progression: Year 1: 36 EC common courses and 24 EC in a single approved four-course language sequence, with entry level and course order respected. The beginner Italian sequence is an eligible example with courses in periods 1, 2, 4 and 5. The dated catalogue also lists two zero-credit requirements.

Year 2: 18 EC common, 18 EC compulsory within European Culture, 12 EC second-major coursework and 12 EC restricted European Culture electives. An eligible example takes Institutional and Substantive Law of the EU alongside Articulating Europe in periods 1–2, the workshop in period 3, then Culture Wars in period 4 and Post-colonial Encounters in period 5. A complete first year clears the 48 EC conditions.

Year 3: 12 EC advanced themes and 6 EC seminar, 30 EC free electives and 12 EC thesis. Democracy and Truth and Europe in Migration are separate eligible courses with the first-year and major-course prerequisites met through year 1 and Articulating Europe. Course registration and future timetable determine free-choice distribution. A seminar in period 4 precedes the thesis in periods 5–6. The catalogue thesis entry requires first-year completion, 30 EC preceding major courses and seminar registration. The approved year-two choices and year-three progression meet the threshold.
